judged_text: Attendees are committed to the DB before updateCalendarAttendees runs and that call is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar provider failure returns a 500 after the DB is mutated with no rollback and no emails sent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no `try/catch` and no DB transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., calendar provider/API failure), the TRPC mutation will reject and the client will see an error while the database has already been mutated (no rollback). Because `sendAddGuestsEmails` happens after that call, it will also not run in this failure path (the email `try/catch` does not cover the calendar update).
